title: Platform governance commitments and statutory remedy routes do not establish worker-level protection
source_unit: Malaysia Act 872 official governance route and Grab Malaysia public response page; comparative institutional layer, not worker sample
geography: Malaysia; comparative platform-governance case used in the US-centered atlas

observations.period: 2026-03-27; Grab Malaysia public Act 872 response page

service_agreement_commitment.unit: clear Terms of Service agreements claimed

earnings_framework_commitment.unit: fair and transparent earnings framework claimed

appeal_and_discipline_commitment.unit: appeal, strike, and dispute-resolution processes described

social_protection_commitment.unit: SOCSO co-contribution and registration support described

partner_program_amount.unit: Malaysian ringgit reported for partner protection and empowerment

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the company's public Act 872 response page; reported commitments are not treated as worker uptake or compliance.
observations.uncertainty: No worker denominator, appeal use, changed decision, access restoration, earnings receipt, SOCSO enrollment, durability, trust, or exit is disclosed on the page.
observations.subgroup: Grab Malaysia platform partners; public company-response surface.
observations.counterinterpretation: A company-reported policy and program amount can coexist with unknown uptake, implementation, appeal outcomes, and worker protection.

observations.period: 2026-09-18; Malaysia Ministry Act 872 and JTKSM implementation route recheck

act_and_tribunal_route_present.unit: Act, subsidiary regulations, Tribunal information, and e-Aduan route exposed

public_case_identifier_observed.unit: public case identifiers for the reported GrabCar proceeding located

public_award_or_payment_observed.unit: public awards, payments, or enforcement outcomes located

observations.method: Targeted review of the official Ministry Act 872 portal, download/implementation page, JTKSM enforcement page, and linked Tribunal route.
observations.uncertainty: A maintained official route can contain private or non-indexed case files; public non-observation is not evidence that no claim or outcome exists.
observations.subgroup: Malaysia gig-worker statutory and enforcement route.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal route availability is institutional capacity, not claimant access, timely adjudication, payment, correction, or durable protection.

observations.period: 2026-09-18; Gig Workers Tribunal procedural regulation route

settlement_award_capability.unit: agreed settlement can be recorded as an award

hearing_to_award_period.unit: days where practicable from last hearing

actual_grabcar_case_outcome_observed.unit: reported GrabCar case awards, payment, or enforcement outcomes located

observations.method: Official regulation and implementation-route review; procedural capability is separated from an actual case file.
observations.uncertainty: The regulation does not identify whether the reported GrabCar matter reached an award, settlement, payment, or enforcement stage.
observations.subgroup: Malaysia Gig Workers Tribunal procedural framework.
observations.counterinterpretation: A legal remedy architecture may remain unused, inaccessible, delayed, or unresolved for a particular worker.

related_sources.claim: Bounded company-response extraction and public-page hash.
Official-route recheck preserving public availability and missing case-outcome fields.

boundary: This is a comparative Malaysia platform-governance layer, not a US worker prevalence estimate or a compliance audit. It distinguishes company commitments, official route capacity, procedural rules, actual case identification, worker uptake, appeal, payment, access restoration, durability, trust, and exit.
